The idea of label smoothing was first proposed to train Inception-v2 [26]. It changes the construction of the true probability to
qi = { 1 − ε if i = y, ε/(K − 1) otherwise,  (4)
where ε is a small constant. Now the optimal solution becomes
z ∗ i = { log((K − 1)(1 − ε)/ε) + α if i = y, α otherwise,  (5)
where α can be an arbitrary real number. This encourages a finite output from the fully-connected layer and can generalize better.

We show that label smoothing impairs distillation, i.e., when teacher models are trained with label smoothing, student models perform worse. We further show that this adverse effect results from loss of information in the logits.

abstract.text: In the airbench94 ~10-epoch CIFAR-10 testbed, test-time augmentation was consequential: removing all TTA cost 0.738 points, while removing translation cost 0.236 points, confirming the paper’s crop-based performance claim [S2][S8][hl_193fdd44b77cd074275ad6e176c7012a]. Patch-whitening initialization was similarly important, with ablation costing 1.276 points [S4][hl_7cc061c7463f10a7ec432d498aac2595]. Label smoothing produced a statistically significant but small 0.078-point gain [S10][hl_33c941e6438e93e3bb07a030aca138fa]. Mixup did not transfer to this short-budget setting: α=1.0 hurt at ~10, 35, and 40 epochs, whereas α=0.2 at 20 and 40 epochs was only inconclusive [S1][S5][S9][S7][S11][hl_0c73f204787e1043e26d4b984a8756c2]. Alternating flips were not established as better; random flips differed by only -0.087 to -0.090 points with intervals spanning zero [S3][S6][hl_f00e337c8a98ab91885e251883ed6dd3]. Human feedback redirected the study toward longer and lower-alpha mixup tests and extra flip seeds rather than prematurely accepting noise-level effects [S3][S1][S5][S9].
findings: Mixup at α=1.0 should improve accuracy → ~10-epoch test → result -1.668 points (95% CI: -2.028 to -1.308) → refuted → α=1.0 mixup was substantially harmful under the airbench budget → open question: whether paper-like 200-epoch training or a different setup would reverse this [S1][hl_0c73f204787e1043e26d4b984a8756c2][hl_50d0a13772972038598976aba67aef0c]

Removing TTA should hurt → TTA-level ablation → result -0.738 points (95% CI: -0.848 to -0.628) → confirmed → test-time views materially improve measured validation accuracy → open question: whether the gain justifies added inference cost [S2][hl_193fdd44b77cd074275ad6e176c7012a]

Alternating flips should outperform random flips → paired flip comparison → result -0.087 points (95% CI: -0.189 to 0.015) → inconclusive → the claimed advantage was not distinguishable from noise → open question: whether additional paired seeds resolve the ~0.1-point effect [S3][hl_f00e337c8a98ab91885e251883ed6dd3]

Patch-whitening initialization should help → remove whitening → result -1.276 points (95% CI: -1.538 to -1.014) → confirmed → whitening is a major contributor in this setup → open question: how much of the benefit is optimization speed versus final accuracy [S4][hl_7cc061c7463f10a7ec432d498aac2595]

Mixup at α=1.0 should recover with 40 epochs → 40-epoch test → result -0.278 points (95% CI: -0.483 to -0.073) → refuted → extending training to 40 epochs did not rescue α=1.0 → open question: whether substantially longer training is required [S5][hl_07db8d8d60e86170dda2cc24919b3c35]

Alternating flips should outperform random flips at a longer budget → 20-epoch paired comparison → result -0.090 points (95% CI: -0.234 to 0.054) → inconclusive → direction matched the claim but evidence remained insufficient → open question: whether more seeds establish the small effect [S6][hl_f00e337c8a98ab91885e251883ed6dd3]

Lower-alpha mixup should improve with extension → α=0.2 for 20 epochs → result 0.088 points (95% CI: -0.053 to 0.229) → inconclusive → a possible small gain was near the noise floor → open question: whether longer training produces a reliable benefit [S7][hl_07db8d8d60e86170dda2cc24919b3c35]

Removing translation should hurt → reduce TTA from level 2 to level 1 → result -0.236 points (95% CI: -0.41 to -0.062) → confirmed → translation views contribute independently to accuracy → open question: the accuracy–inference-time tradeoff [S8][hl_193fdd44b77cd074275ad6e176c7012a]

Mixup at α=1.0 should improve at 35 epochs → 35-epoch test → result -0.462 points (95% CI: -0.571 to -0.353) → refuted → repeated α=1.0 failures argue against this configuration through 35 epochs → open question: whether the reported 200-epoch regime is essential [S9][hl_50d0a13772972038598976aba67aef0c]

Label smoothing at ε=0.1 should improve → label-smoothing ablation → result 0.078 points (95% CI: 0.024 to 0.132) → confirmed → it gave a small but statistically supported gain → open question: whether the gain persists across seeds and budgets [S10][hl_33c941e6438e93e3bb07a030aca138fa]

Lower-alpha mixup should improve at 40 epochs → α=0.2, 40-epoch test → result 0.248 points (95% CI: -0.004 to 0.5) → inconclusive → this was promising but narrowly missed clear evidence → open question: whether additional seeds or longer training confirm the apparent benefit [S11][hl_07db8d8d60e86170dda2cc24919b3c35]

claims.conditions: On CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, the paper compares PreAct ResNet-18, WideResNet-28-10, and DenseNet-BC-190 (growth rate 40), trained for 200 epochs on a single Tesla P100 with batch size 128; mixup uses alpha=1, weight decay 1e-4, no dropout, and learning-rate decays at epochs 100 and 150 (WideResNet: 60, 120, and 180). abstract.text: In the airbench94 ~10-epoch CIFAR-10 testbed, test-time augmentation was consequential: removing all TTA cost 0.738 points, while removing translation cost 0.236 points, confirming the paper’s crop-based performance claim [S2][S8][hl_193fdd44b77cd074275ad6e176c7012a]. Patch-whitening initialization was similarly important, with ablation costing 1.276 points [S4][hl_7cc061c7463f10a7ec432d498aac2595]. Label smoothing produced a statistically significant but small 0.078-point gain [S10][hl_33c941e6438e93e3bb07a030aca138fa]. Mixup did not transfer to this short-budget setting: α=1.0 hurt at ~10, 35, and 40 epochs, whereas α=0.2 at 20 and 40 epochs was only inconclusive [S1][S5][S9][S7][S11][hl_0c73f204787e1043e26d4b984a8756c2]. Alternating flips were not established as better; random flips differed by only -0.087 to -0.090 points with intervals spanning zero [S3][S6][hl_f00e337c8a98ab91885e251883ed6dd3]. Human feedback redirected the study toward longer and lower-alpha mixup tests and extra flip seeds rather than prematurely accepting noise-level effects [S3][S1][S5][S9].
